\label{lesson:KA-C208-deha}

\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ದೇಹ}}
\textbf{\kn{ದೇಹ}} — \emph{dēha} — \textquotedblleft{}the body\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ದೇಹ}} (\emph{dēha}) is Sanskrit \emph{deha}, \textquotedblleft{}body\textquotedblright{}, taken over whole as a learned loan, a tatsama (CDIAL 6557).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಚುಚ್ಚುಮದ್ದು} (cuccumaddu)}{ಚುಚ್ಚುಮದ್ದು (cuccumaddu)}]{\kn{ಚುಚ್ಚುಮದ್ದು} (cuccumaddu) — an injection}

Before the new one: say the Kannada for to collect, then the Kannada for the body.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಚುಚ್ಚುಮದ್ದು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಚುಚ್ಚುಮದ್ದು}} — \emph{cuccumaddu} — \textquotedblleft{}an injection\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಚುಚ್ಚುಮದ್ದು}} (\emph{cuccumaddu}) is native Dravidian: \emph{cuccu}, \textquotedblleft{}to insert, put in as on a spit\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 2778), and \emph{maddu}, \textquotedblleft{}medicine\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4719, with Tamil \emph{maruntu}): \textquotedblleft{}medicine pushed in\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
